requirements.summary: Recovery locus — one startup-phase mutator. Recovery is exactly one new `Store` method, `RecoverRejected`, called **once per process** by `cmd/mcp-bridge/serve.go` immediately after `storage.Open` succeeds and before any admission/loop work. It is the only code path that creates or prunes quarantine files. `Load`, `Save`, `LoadPrompts`, `SavePrompts`, and `ensureReplaceable` keep today's observable behavior byte-for-byte and never quarantine.

Quarantine-once byte preservation. Per family, a store-rejected file is moved exactly once via `os.Rename` into the same state directory under a bounded conforming quarantine name; bytes are preserved (rename, never delete/truncate/overwrite-first); the configured path is absent afterwards; a file that loads is never moved; the target of a symlinked entry is never touched.

Fatal classes. A directory at a family path (including a symlink resolving to a directory), a rename failure, a reservation-create failure, a post-rename directory-sync failure, and exhaustion of the 4096 reservation attempts are **fatal**: `RecoverRejected` returns an error wrapping the new sentinel `storage.ErrSnapshotUnrecoverable` and the real cause; `serve.go` maps it to the existing `stateDirectoryFailure(state dir)`, so `runContext` writes exactly one `startup_failed` record (`code=state_directory`, `kind=resource`, `resource.path`). Nothing is overwritten on the fatal path.

Typed warning records. Each completed quarantine yields exactly one stderr `startup_snapshot_rejected` record: level `warn`, operation `startup`, outcome `degraded`, `error.code=snapshot_unavailable` (`kind=resource`), `failure_reason` (finite taxonomy), `resource.path`=configured state directory, `quarantine_path`=absolute quarantine path. Retention failures yield one `snapshot_retention_failed` record each (`warn`/`startup`/`failure`, `code=state_directory`). No `startup_failed` and no `internal_error` is emitted for the recoverable path. Records for completed recoveries are emitted **before** any fatal return.

Retention bounds. Per family, at most `QuarantineKeep` (5) newest **conforming** quarantine files are retained; pruning runs only for a family that created a quarantine this run; this run's own file is never pruned; non-conforming and offset-form names are never counted or touched; prune/listing/unlink failures are reported as non-fatal `RetentionFailure` entries, never silently ignored.

Reason taxonomy. `Recovery.Reason` is a five-value closed vocabulary — `corrupt_json`, `checksum_mismatch`, `unsupported_schema`, `validation_failure`, `read_error` — derived deterministically from the same branch walk `Load`/`LoadPrompts` exercise: every schema-1 branch failure (decode, trailing data, frozen-checksum mismatch) is `corrupt_json`; `checksum_mismatch` is produced only by the schema-2 checksum sentinel; unreadable paths (read or unclassified stat errors) are `read_error`.

Opt-out. `MCP_SNAPSHOT_QUARANTINE` defaults **ON** (unset ⇒ enabled). The value `off`, compared case-insensitively and exactly, is the only disabled spelling (fail-closed opt-out for manual-inspection deployments). When disabled, no recovery runs, no file is renamed, and **no** recovery or retention record of any kind is emitted; today's behavior is retained.

Envelope vocabulary evolution. The shared envelope gains the optional event-specific field `quarantine_path`; the existing `failure_reason` field's admitted vocabulary is extended with the five snapshot reasons; `snapshot_unavailable` and `state_directory` join the closed runtime error classification; the new event `snapshot_retention_failed` gets a fixed message. All are optional event-specific additions: `schema_version` stays 1, no field is removed/renamed/retyped. `docs/logging-contract.md` union and tables are updated; the `EnvelopeFieldNames` count pin moves 129→130.

Continue startup and self-heal. After recovery, startup proceeds with no restored catalog/prompt state, admission persists and publishes a fresh valid `snapshot.json`, the loop's async initial refresh republishes `prompts.json` (`internal/service/loop.go:172` `Trigger()`; admission skips `PersistPrompts`, `internal/service/reload.go:728`), and a second run against the same state directory is a no-op (no new quarantine file, no new record).
